messages:
samir: FYI — Acme reported embeddings throughput drop this morning. vectors/sec down ~70% since 06:10 UTC, tokens/sec flat. They hit SLA. Logs attached.

olivia: Can you paste the numbers? model id? logs? :eyes:

samir: model: rwd-embed-v1-1, region: us-west-2. vectors/sec before 25k -> now 7.6k. tokens/sec steady ~210k. No 5xx. No auth errors. Customer timeline and curl repro below.

samir: ```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer ${KEY}" \
  -d '{"input": ["text1","text2"], "model":"rwd-embed-v1-1"}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings
``` 

luis: Any recent routing or batching rollout? I see a deploy earlier by ingrid at 05:58 (autoscaler/batch-window tuning). deploy-bot: deployed autoscaler/batch-window v2.1 to us-west-2 canary.

ingrid: rolled batch-window change to canary (reduce max-batch-size from 64 -> 16 to reduce latency p99). I did not extend to prod. :wave:

olivia: That change would shrink batches and could kill vectors throughput even if token stream looks fine. If batches drop, vectorization effective throughput drops. Can we check queue depth + average batch size in us-west-2?

luis: Traces: queue_depth spiked to 210 -> gpu-queue-saturation, avg_batch_size fell from 42 -> 9. KV cache hit remained ~90%. Attached flame log snippet:

luis: ```
metric: avg_batch_size  timestamps: [05:00: 42, 06:00: 9]
metric: gpu_queue_depth [05:00: 18, 06:00: 210]
``` 

olivia: That matches. Also see increased small-batch overhead — kernel launch cost dominates for vector pipeline. Suggest rollback or change policy to bin small requests into "vec-batch-cohort".

ingrid: I'll roll canary back and bump max-batch-size to 48 in prod now. Rolling rollback to canary -> 06:40 UTC.

deploy-bot: rollback completed: autoscaler/batch-window v2.0 -> us-west-2 canary at 06:42 UTC

luis: After rollback avg_batch_size climbed to 39, vectors/sec back to ~23k. tokens/sec unchanged. :thumbsup:

samir: I'll update customer with repro steps and ETA. Thanks team. I'll keep thread open for 1h to monitor.

olivia: For follow-up, let's add load-aware batch-coalescing to avoid small-batch collapse (ticket INF-2345). Also add a watch for avg_batch_size < 12 with alert. :memo:

samir: noted. pinging @support-customer-success to tell Acme. :phone:
